# NVGT

NVGT (NonVisual Gaming Toolkit) is a scripting engine for building audio games. Scripts are `.nvgt` files written in a dialect of **AngelScript**, run or compiled by the `nvgt` executable.

This skill bundles a complete copy of NVGT's documentation and a generated dump of its engine API, so it works without the NVGT source tree present. See `reference/SOURCE.md` for the exact version bundled.

## The one rule that matters

**Never write an NVGT signature from memory. Look it up first.**

NVGT's API is large (192 types, ~5200 methods, 565 global functions) and full of names that *look* like C++, BGT, Python or plain AngelScript but differ in arity, defaults or return type. Guessing produces code that looks right and does not compile.

Lookup order:

1. **`reference/engine-api.md`** — generated by asking the engine to serialize its own registered API. Exact, complete, authoritative. Grep it for the symbol.
2. **`reference/api-index.md`** — maps every documented symbol to its prose doc file under `reference/docs/`. Read that file for semantics, remarks and a runnable example.
3. **`reference/stdlib/`** — full source of the 29 bundled includes. These are plain NVGT scripts; read them when the docs run out.

When the prose docs and `engine-api.md` disagree, **`engine-api.md` wins** — the prose lags. A live example: the doc for `sound::load` still shows `pack@ soundpack`, while the engine registers `bool load(const string&in filename, const pack_interface@ pack = sound_default_pack)`.

Grep, don't read whole files. `engine-api.md` is 320 KB and `api-index.md` is 126 KB; both are structured for searching.

## Program shape

The entry point is `void main()` or `int main()`. Nothing runs without one.

```nvgt
#include "speech.nvgt"

void main() {
	show_window("My game");
	while (!key_pressed(KEY_ESCAPE)) {
		wait(5);
		if (key_pressed(KEY_SPACE)) speak("Hello!");
	}
}
```

`wait(5)` in every main loop is not optional. On the main thread `wait` also pumps the window, dispatches input events and runs incremental garbage collection. A loop without it hangs the window and pins a CPU core.

A script with no `main()` is an **include script** (NVGT's word for a module), pulled in with `#include`.

## Language

AngelScript, statically typed, C-like syntax, `;` terminated, `{}` blocks. Familiar from C++/Java: `if`/`else`, `while`, `for`, `do`, `switch`, `break`, `continue`, classes with `private`/`public`, `const`, function overloading, default arguments, `interface`, `enum`, exceptions via `try`/`catch`.

What you must get right because it differs from what habit suggests:

**Handles are `@`, not `*`.** A handle is a reference to a reference-counted object.

```nvgt
sound@ s = sound();       // handle to a new sound
sound@ other = @s;        // @ on the right hand side takes a handle
if (@s == null) return;   // null check
mixer@ m = cast<mixer@>(obj);   // downcast with cast<T@>(), not (T*)
```

Value types (`string`, `int`, `float`, `vector`, `timer`, …) are copied on assignment and need no `@`.

**`&in`, `&out`, `&inout` are reference parameter modifiers.** `const string&in` is the normal way to take a string parameter; `uint&out` is an out-parameter.

**Arrays.** `T[]` and `array<T>` are the same type; `T[]` is a shorthand AngelScript grants to one chosen template class.

```nvgt
string[] items = {"a", "b", "c"};
array<int> nums(10);
items.length();     // METHOD, not a property — array.length is a compile error
items[-1];          // legal in NVGT: last element
```

Out-of-bounds access **throws**, it does not return a sentinel. Guard with `length()` or catch it.

**Strings are objects with methods**, not targets of global functions. `s.length()`, `s.split(...)`, `s.replace(...)`, `s.upper()`, `s.find(...)`, `s.substr(...)`, `s.slice(...)`. `+` concatenates, and concatenating a number to a string converts it automatically.

**Virtual properties are `get_`/`set_` methods marked `property`, accessed without the prefix.** This is why `engine-api.md` is full of `get_volume() const property` — in script you write `s.volume`. Declaring one yourself *requires* the prefix; `bool alive() const property` is a compile error ("Invalid signature for virtual property").

```nvgt
class enemy {
	float health = 100;
	bool get_alive() const property { return health > 0; }
}
enemy e;
if (e.alive) { }   // no parentheses, no get_
```

**Numeric types:** `int`/`uint` are 32-bit, plus `int8/16/64`, `uint8/16/64`, `float`, `double`, `bool`. There is also a dynamic `var` type — so never name a variable `var`.

**Containers:** `array<T>`, `dictionary`, `grid<T>`. `dictionary` is string-keyed and stores `any`; retrieve with a typed cast or use `dget.nvgt`.

Indentation in NVGT's own code is **tabs**. Match it.

## Preprocessor

`#` directives are resolved before compilation.

```nvgt
#include "speech.nvgt"      // include path: script's own dir first, then NVGT's include folder
#pragma plugin nvgt_sqlite  // load a plugin by dll basename
```

Directives worth knowing:

| Directive | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `#include "file.nvgt"` | Include another script. **Code only** — unlike BGT, this cannot embed packs. |
| `#pragma include <dir>` | Add a directory to the include search path (repeatable) |
| `#pragma embed <pack>` | Embed a pack file into the compiled executable (multiple allowed) |
| `#pragma asset <path>` | Copy assets into the bundled product |
| `#pragma document <path>` | Copy files in as user-facing documents |
| `#pragma plugin <name>` | Load and activate a plugin |
| `#pragma compiled_basename <name>` | Output filename without extension |
| `#pragma console` | Build with the Windows console subsystem (CLI programs) |
| `#pragma stub <name>` | Choose the compilation stub |

Conditional compilation uses `#if <word>` / `#if_not <word>` / `#endif`, plus `#define <word>`. Note it tests **whether a word is defined**, not an expression. Words defined automatically: the target platform (`windows`, `linux`, `mac`, `android`, `ios`), `mobile` or `desktop`, `plugin_<name>` for each loaded plugin, and `include` inside an included file.

```nvgt
#if windows
	// windows-only code
#endif
#if_not plugin_legacy_sound
	pack_file@ pack_file = null;
#endif
```

## Audio-game idioms

- **Speech.** `#include "speech.nvgt"` then `speak("text")` — it routes to the active screen reader if one is running and falls back to TTS otherwise. That is what you want by default. Use `screen_reader_speak` / `tts_voice` directly only when you specifically need one or the other. NVGT auto-detects the screen reader; you never name it.
- **Sound.** `sound` is the core class: `load(filename)`, `play()`, `play_looped()`, `play_wait()`, `stop()`, `pause()`, and properties `volume`, `pan`, `pitch`, `playing`, `active`, `length`. `set_position(...)` places it in 3D relative to a listener. `load()` already combines streaming and preloading — there is no separate `stream()` worth calling.
- **Many overlapping sounds.** Use `sound_pool.nvgt` rather than juggling `sound@` handles by hand.
- **Menus and forms.** `menu.nvgt` for list menus, `form.nvgt` (`audio_form`) for richer accessible UI. Don't hand-roll either.
- **Saved settings.** `settings.nvgt` writes config files (INI/JSON/properties). It does not touch the registry.
- **Timing.** The `timer` class: `timer.elapsed`, `has_elapsed(n)`, `restart()`, `pause()`/`resume()`. Its internal clock is microsecond-accurate but the units your script sees are set by the global `timer_default_accuracy`, which defaults to `MILLISECONDS` — read it before assuming a unit. For frame pacing, `wait(5)`.
- **Text entry.** `get_characters()` once per loop iteration returns everything typed since the last call, including IME and emoji input — that is how you build a virtual text field. `key_pressed` is edge-triggered (this frame), `key_down` is level-triggered (held).

## Running and compiling

```bash
nvgt game.nvgt                    # run
nvgt -c game.nvgt                 # compile, release
nvgt -C game.nvgt                 # compile with debug info
nvgt -c -pwindows game.nvgt       # target a platform (auto|android|windows|linux|mac|ios)
nvgt -d game.nvgt                 # run under the AngelScript debugger
nvgt -w1 game.nvgt                # print script warnings (0 ignore, 1 print, 2 error)
```

On Windows, right-clicking a `.nvgt` file in Explorer offers "compile script (release)".

By default NVGT **bundles** the whole game — executable, sounds, libraries, documents — into a zip or platform equivalent. Set `build.windows_bundle = 0` in `config.properties` next to `nvgt.exe` for a bare executable instead (then you may need to ship libraries from `lib/` yourself).

Configuration files are read from, in order: `<script_basename>.{ini,json,properties}` next to the script, `.nvgtrc` in that directory or any parent, `<exe_basename>.{ini,json,properties}` in NVGT's directory or a parent, then `config.{ini,json,properties}` there.

Read `reference/docs/manual/compiling your project for distribution.md` before advising on shipping a real game.

## Mistakes to avoid

| Wrong | Right |
| --- | --- |
| `array.length` | `array.length()` |
| `string_len(s)`, `string_split(s)` | `s.length()`, `s.split(...)` |
| `sound* s = new sound()` | `sound@ s = sound();` |
| `(mixer@)obj` | `cast<mixer@>(obj)` |
| Main loop with no `wait(5)` | Always `wait(5)` |
| `#include "pack.dat"` | `#pragma embed pack.dat` |
| `KEY_PRIOR`, `KEY_LCONTROL` | `KEY_PAGEUP`, `KEY_LCTRL` |
| Naming a variable `var` | `var` is a type in NVGT |
| Assuming a signature | Grep `reference/engine-api.md` |

Porting from BGT is common and has its own long list of renamed functions and changed key constants: read `reference/docs/manual/-BGT Upgrading+.md`. `#include "bgt_compat.nvgt"` provides aliases as a stopgap.

## Keeping this current

The bundled docs are frozen at the version in `reference/SOURCE.md`. If the user's NVGT is newer, say so rather than asserting stale details. Regenerate with:

```bash
python tools/build_skill.py /path/to/nvgt-repo
```
